edit.description: classify the `loop` arm's `liveLoopPid` read like its stop-flag sibling above it
refusal case beside the loop stop-flag one

summary: `flume loop`'s prior-holder probe classifies a present-but-unreadable loop.pid instead of exiting 1 over a raw stack
acceptance: `flume loop` against a loop.pid that stats and will not open prints a `[flume] loop refuses:` line naming the read failure and exits EX_IOERR; no lock and no tip claim are left behind
tests: `flume loop` refuses naming the error when loop.pid is present but unreadable, instead of exiting 1 over a raw stack
notes: src/cli.ts:1250 calls `liveLoopPid` outside any try; it answers null for absent and rethrows every other read failure, so EISDIR reaches `main()`'s catch — exit 1, the same code as `another loop (pid N) already runs`, with no pid named. Sibling stop-flag guard ~110 lines up already returns EX_IOERR, and `flume status` shipped the identical shape for the same file. Independent of questions/does-flume-tick-s-exit-range-admit-ex-ioerr.md: loop already returns 74 here.
